precepts.text: Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on nothing else.
precepts.point: The commentary says it plainly: false teachers who sound impressive, grand, polished, even spiritual, but hollow; style over truth, eloquence without substance.
precepts.why:
Paul warned of them: “by good words and fair speeches deceive the hearts of the simple.” Good words and fair speeches: intellectual, big words, semantics, rhetoric. They serve theology; their theology is their god, and their own belly, money. Peter says the same: “For when they speak great swelling words of vanity, they allure through the lusts of the flesh”. There are no laws involved, no commandments involved.

The commentary on Peter says it: false teachers who sound impressive yet deliver nothing of substance. Homoousios, hypostatic, exegesis, ontological, hermeneutical, Christological: great swelling words. Their speech is grand, polished, well paced, even spiritual sounding, like Bible, but it is hollow, with no commandments, no responsibility, no accountability. Unlike Paul, who said “my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power”. Paul refused persuasive words of man's wisdom; these teachers rely on style over truth, eloquence without gospel substance. In the Greek, great swelling words means great bulk: high sounding, but only words, vain and meaningless, with nothing but emptiness behind them.

Show me the scripture that says Christ is fully God and fully man. It isn't there. The word of God is plain and clear. Even their hermeneutics goes back to Schleiermacher, a German called the father of modern liberal theology, and Isaiah says “The vile person shall be no more called liberal”; the vile person will “utter error against the Lord, to make empty the soul of the hungry”. The word comes from Hermes, the Greek trickster god, so it is a trickster's interpretation, and the Jesuits carried it around the earth.

Peel back the swelling words and here is the premise: if Christ is fully God and fully man, only a two-essence being can keep God's laws, so we don't have to. But Christ said be perfect, as your Father in heaven is perfect, and Zacharias and Elisabeth walked “in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless.” It can be done. “The discourse of fools is irksome, and their sport is the wantonness of sin”: their sport is not having to keep the commandments.

precepts.text: Remember the scripture says a spiritual man discerneth all things.
precepts.point: Now, let me say this now. Remember the scripture says a spiritual man discerneth all things. You can hear. Where's that one in Sirach? Divers meats. No, no, no. False speeches. Yeah. Yeah, that's it. A palate. That's it. I forgot it. Oh, Sirach 36. Hold this. We're going to come right back here. Sirach 36:19.

note.label: From Milk to Meat: Train All Your Senses

precepts.why:
Ananias and Sapphira sold a possession and “kept back part of the price”. It was their property anyway; they did not have to lie. But Peter said, “Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost, and to keep back part of the price of the land?”

Nobody had to tell Peter that. He already knew. That was the spirit of God working those senses. When he saw him, he already knew something was not right with this man, something was not right with this spirit: you are dealing evil right now. That is what the scripture means: “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things”. A spiritual man discerns all things.

Sirach shows how that discerning works: “As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” When you eat, you do not have to see; you can tell the difference between chicken and beef, chicken and fish, without looking. So a heart of understanding can discern false speech. One way: a man who is talking too much. You do not have to convince anyone of the truth.

Peter told him, “thou hast not lied unto men, but unto God.” And “Ananias hearing these words fell down, and gave up the ghost: and great fear came on all them that heard these things.” The fear came because Peter was able to discern lies and truth. We laugh about it because we know it is true: when you are not moving right and a brother in the spirit sees it, you wonder how he knew. That is clear knowing, the spiritual senses trained and at work.

precepts.text: Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect. So the wisdom that we are speaking among these people out here that think they have got some real wisdom. Yet not the wisdom of this world. We do not speak their wisdom. We speak God's wisdom. God's commandments. That is how we speak. Nor of the princes of this world. We do not speak the wisdom of the princes of this world. Their wisdom is not God's wisdom. That come to nought. That come to nothing. The Lord is going to bring all that wisdom down. It is our wisdom that is going to be raised up in authority in this society.
precepts.point: For in her is an understanding spirit, holy, one only, manifold, subtle, lively, clear, undefiled. The wisdom of God is undefiled. Plain, not subject to hurt. It is not subject to hurt. Loving the thing that is good, quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good. The wisdom will lead us to be proper in everything, everywhere we seek to move, everything that we seek to endeavour, everything that we seek to make happen. Wisdom will properly guide us. Not just any kind of wisdom. God's wisdom. I have got to clarify that.

note.label: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

precepts.why:
Wisdom is “loving the thing that is good quick, which cannot be letted, ready to do good”. That wisdom will properly guide us in everything we seek to move in, every endeavour, everything we seek to make happen. But not just any kind of wisdom: God’s wisdom. Paul makes that clear.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect”. We speak wisdom among these people out here who think they have some real wisdom. “Yet not the wisdom of this world”: we do not speak their wisdom. We speak God’s wisdom, God’s commandments; that is how we speak.

“Nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought”. The wisdom of the princes of this world is not God’s wisdom, and it comes to nothing. The Lord is going to bring all that wisdom down, and it is our wisdom that is going to be raised up in authority in this society.

That is the difference between God’s wisdom and what we learned under Christianity, clapping with a Bible while learning nothing about ourselves, our condition, our deliverance or our salvation, and still having white supremacy on the mind. The wisdom of this world taught us to look at ourselves as nothing, and everything behind that was destroyed. God’s wisdom is “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” That breath has to come in, as in Ezekiel 37 when “the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army”, and undo all that damage.

precepts.text: That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God: the power of God is the word of God. We do not speak the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought; the princes of this world are the nations. We speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory. What we are saying seems so unheard of: it is only for the Israelites, Christ is black, it is about gathering the twelve tribes back together. It is hidden. Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory. If the scribes and Pharisees had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right; but they followed Rome. Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him: what God has prepared is unimaginable.
precepts.point: In whom are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge: in the Father and in Christ are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
precepts.why:
In the Father and in Christ “are hid all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.” Paul explains that hidden wisdom to the Corinthians: “That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God.” Do not let your faith stand in the wisdom of men, the ones who speak very well with six syllable words, quoting poets and philosophers. The power of God is the word of God.

“Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world, nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought.” The wisdom of this world says, give us reparations and it will solve all our problems; a lot of black people have hit the lotto and accomplished zero. The princes of this world are the nations.

“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory.” The world does not know it, so what we are saying seems unheard of: it is only for the Israelites? Christ is black and you are going to rule the world? It is about gathering the twelve tribes back together? It is hidden, and it was ordained before the world for our glory.

“Which none of the princes of this world knew: for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.” The scribes and Pharisees followed and obeyed Rome. If they had followed God the Father through the Son, they would have been all right.

“But as it is written, Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him.” Brothers and sisters in AI create beautiful things, but what God has prepared no one has ever seen or heard of; it is unimaginable. “But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. That is the treasure hid in Christ.

precepts.text: My speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man's wisdom, because man's wisdom can beguile you, deceive you.
precepts.point: On family: we do not break up families. If your family does not have an issue with you being in the scriptures and is not trying to manipulate your children, fine. But we will warn you if your family is saying come out of that Bible and go back to what you used to do. They will seduce you to go right back to the way you used to be, because that is what the scribes and the Pharisees were doing, and that is what the Christian preachers do.
precepts.why:
Paul warns “lest any man should beguile you with enticing words.” To beguile is to charm, enchant or attract someone, sometimes in a deceptive or cunning way; the word bridges a line between friendly charm and sneaky manipulation.

What are those enticing words? They go back to the wisdom of this world. Paul says of himself: “And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words of man’s wisdom”. Why? Because man's wisdom can beguile you and deceive you.

Paul was not pulling things out of thin air. What he taught he got from the scriptures, the Old Testament, and “God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God.” Paul had many visions and saw wonders. So the preaching that does not beguile is the word revealed by the spirit, not the enticing words of man's wisdom.

precepts.text: Paul speaks of understanding all mysteries.
precepts.point: The natural man cannot receive or know the things of the Spirit.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery, even the hidden wisdom”. Paul was one who understood that mystery. He wrote: “And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains”.

Prophecy is a gift, and Paul had the gift of prophecy. He understood all mysteries. That is why, when we read the book of Hebrews, we understand a lot of things in Genesis: because of the letters of Paul. Paul explained a lot of things and took them to another level, making them plain for us, even things in the law that we do not fully understand.

He had all knowledge and all faith. So when Paul says “we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery”, he is speaking as a man who was given to understand the mysteries, the hidden wisdom which God ordained before the world unto our glory. That hidden wisdom goes into Christ: who he was and who he is was hid from our people for all ages, and even the princes of this world did not know it, “for had they known it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.”

precepts.text: It is not given to everyone to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.
precepts.point: The natural man cannot receive or know the things of the Spirit.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Christ said: “Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” It is given to the apostles and certain men to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; it is not given to everyone. Once these men understand it, God having revealed it to them, they reveal it to the people and the people understand it. It is given to the apostles first and foremost.

That is the wisdom of God in a mystery, the hidden wisdom. There is hidden wisdom even about Adam: did Adam have a kingdom? People think he was running around butt naked. No; it is hidden wisdom.

“but to them it is not given”. That is why there is no need to argue with anybody about what the scriptures mean. Correct them and keep it moving. If God did not open your eyes, you are not going to get it. As Paul says, “the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” So why try to force him to know it? Correct them and dust off your shoes, because everyone is not going to get the things of the Spirit of God.

precepts.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments, and the Comforter will teach you all things.
precepts.point: The natural man cannot receive or know the things of the Spirit.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man, the things which God hath prepared for them that love him. But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit”. Who are those that love him? Christ said: “If ye love me, keep my commandments.”

There are two types of people in this world: people who say they love God, like the Christians who all say they love the Lord and love Jesus, and people who do what Jesus said. Which one is justified? If you are not doing what he said and you say you love him, you are a liar.

To the ones who keep his commandments he sends the Spirit: “And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever”. And: “But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance”. That is how we learn the different levels of understanding in the scriptures; it starts with the apostles, and they teach the people.

So we do not teach with man's wisdom from a theology school or seminary; we teach “which the Holy Ghost teacheth; comparing spiritual things with spiritual.” The things God has prepared for us, the holy city, living forever, being with Christ even if we die keeping the commandments, are on another level. They are freely given to us of God; we just have to keep his commandments.

precepts.text: I determined not to know anything among you, save Jesus Christ and him crucified.
precepts.point: Violence shall no more be heard in the land, and the people shall be all righteous.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
Peter asks, since this whole earth is reserved unto fire, “Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness”. That means we have to act right and speak right. A lot of our conversation is filth and sports. We have to train ourselves to speak the words of this book.

When we came into the school, they used to say about one of the elders: if you weren't talking about the Bible, don't talk to him; that's all he wanted to hear. Paul said the same: “For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified.” He trained himself. All I want to hear is Bible. I don't want to hear Betty got a big booty. I don't want to hear how many touchdowns somebody ran or how far he hit the jump shot. I don't want to hear that crap.

That is holy conversation, and godliness is our actions, our works: the way we live must match the way we speak. The scoffers walk after their own lusts and their conversation follows their lusts. The beloved, knowing the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, train their minds and spirits to know nothing but Christ and him crucified, so that they may be found of him in peace, without spot, and blameless.

precepts.text: He that is spiritual judgeth all things; the spiritual man keeps the commandments.
precepts.point: Judgment did not pass away with the Old Testament. He that is spiritual judgeth all things, and the spiritual man is the man that keeps the commandments. The saints shall judge the world, so brethren should judge the smallest matters among themselves instead of going to law before the unjust; only matters of life and death under today's system go outside.

note.label: Exodus 18: Jethro's Counsel and Righteous Leadership

precepts.why:
Judgment did not pass away with the Old Testament. Paul writes, “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.” The spiritual man is the man that keeps the commandments.

That is who Jethro told Moses to look for: able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness. Men like that are spiritual, and the spiritual man judges. The rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens were to judge the people at all seasons, and he that is spiritual still judgeth all things.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 3 A Message to The 7 Churches

precepts.why:
It ain't talking about your physical eyes. “But the natural man” The natural man is the sinful man. “receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God:” The natural man, the sinful man, does not receive the things of the Spirit of God. “for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.” The Bible can only be spiritually discerned. This is a spiritual thing we are in. “But he that is spiritual judgeth all things, yet he himself is judged of no man.”

So we want the Lord to anoint our spiritual eyes with eyesalve so that we can spiritually discern what is written in the Bible. That is our prayer; that is what we want.

points: And I, brethren, when I came to you, came not with excellency of speech. Like they do in the Christian church. They try to speak all proper and they try to use big words.

Or of wisdom, declaring unto you the testimony of God. For I determined not to know any thing among you, save Jesus Christ, and him crucified. That is all Paul was teaching them. Christ died for your sins. Repent and believe on Jesus Christ as your saviour.
And I was with you in weakness, and in fear, and in much trembling. Why? Because they were being persecuted by Rome.

And my speech and my preaching was not with enticing words. I am not trying to say stuff to make you come and join us. In the church they try to give you enticing words. Of man's wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power. Because there is spirit and power in teaching about the black Messiah that died to save the twelve tribes of Israel.
That your faith should not stand in the wisdom of men, but in the power of God. Christian philosophy, Methodist, Baptist, Catholic — that is wisdom of man. That is not according to God's plan.

Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world. We are not telling you Christian ideologies or these religious denominations. That is the wisdom of this world. That is all made up. Nor of the princes of this world. The princes of this world are the ideologies and the thoughts that they give you to keep you away from God, to keep you in debt to them, to make you look up to them. That come to nought. Those people are going to come to nothing.

But we speak the wisdom of God in a mystery. In a what? In a mystery. People are curious. What are they talking about? Why do they have purple and gold on? You have got bums from other churches coming to watch our videos, coming into our chat. You all saw last night. Go somewhere. You do not believe us. Why are you watching us? All night. Men, women, everything. It was three in the morning. You could go watch Netflix. You could go to the club. But they want to hear what we are teaching from the Bible.

They never heard it before. This is wisdom. It is a mystery to them. Even the hidden wisdom, which God ordained before the world unto our glory. The secrets are given to us for our glory. We are telling God's story.

But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit. At that time "us" was the apostles and the believers in Christ: the visions of Jeremiah, of Isaiah, of Daniel were revealed to our forefathers back in that time, the same way they are revealed to us today.
For the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God: those deep things, those parables, those dark sentences, the spirit searches out and shows to us.

The things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God: the Spirit of God understands the things of God and reveals them to us; God's plan for the future, what is going to happen on this earth. The prophets wrote what is going to happen in these last days, and the things you see taking place on this earth, the prophets wrote about. Only the sons of God, the Israelites, can understand these visions, because we have the Spirit of God dwelling in us.
But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
That's the carnal man. He cannot understand this spiritual thing, cannot understand these scriptures. He has no understanding and no wisdom. He cannot be a judge.
